name: State Tree

hero.title: The MobX-State-Tree model, with 9.5× faster actions.
hero.lede: Models with views and actions, JSON snapshots, patches you can record and replay, middleware, references by id. The ideas MobX-State-Tree made popular, built on signals instead of observables, and measured against MST 9 op for op.

facts.value: faster on all 5 published ops<small>2.2× to 9.5×, bun, one run.</small>
Zod, Valibot, ArkType, `s`<small>Schema mode validates every `set`, `patch` and `update`.</small>
{dot:warn}iOS and Android, experimental<small>`model()` compiles to a native singleton.</small>

why.title: For state that has real structure.

items.title: History you don't have to build
items.text: `onSnapshot` hands you plain JSON after each burst of changes (coalesced per microtask), and `applySnapshot` puts it back. Undo, time travel and persistence are an array and two calls.

items.title: Patches out, patches in
items.text: Every write emits a JSON patch with a path like `/profile/name`, nested models included. Send them to a server, log them, or replay them with `applyPatch`.

items.title: Middleware that can say no
items.text: `addMiddleware(node, (call, next) => …)` sees every action with its name and arguments. Don't call `next` and the action never runs: read-only modes, permission checks, audit logs.

items.title: Signals underneath
items.text: Every state field is a `Signal`, every view is read like one. Components bind to `todo.done()` directly, with no `observer()` wrapper and no proxy.

difference.title: Same model, minus the observable machinery.

before.label: MobX-State-Tree 9
before.caption: `types.*` declarations, getters for views, mutation through `self` inside actions.

after.label: with @pyreon/state-tree
after.caption: Plain initial values, views as functions, signals in the actions.

items.name: `model({ state })`
items.text: then `.views()`, `.actions()`, `.volatile()`, `.lifecycle()`; finish with `.create()` or a singleton `.asHook(id)`.

items.name: Schema mode
items.text: `model({ schema })` with `s`, Zod, Valibot or ArkType; `set`, `patch`, `deepPatch`, `update` validate before writing.

items.name: Async actions
items.text: an action can `await`; it is still one action to middleware.

items.name: Volatile state
items.text: reactive, but left out of snapshots and patches.

items.name: Middleware
items.text: `addMiddleware` can block or wrap; `onAction` only observes.

items.name: References
items.text: `identifier()` and `reference(Type)` store an id and resolve to the live node; snapshots keep the id.

api.title: Models, and the functions that watch them.

limits.title: Patches are per field
limits.text: A write replaces a field, so changing one item in an array emits one `replace` of the whole array at `/todos`. MobX-State-Tree emits `/todos/0/done`. Snapshots and undo are unaffected.

limits.title: Keep collections as plain data
limits.text: Hold arrays of plain objects and put the actions on the parent, as the docs' todo example does. A model instance stored inside an array field doesn't yet produce replayable patches; nested models as named fields do.

limits.title: Schema mode is flat
limits.text: Nested models compose in plain mode. A schema-mode model validates its own fields.

limits.title: More structure than a store
limits.text: For a few shared values `@pyreon/store` is less ceremony. Reach for state-tree when you want snapshots, patches or middleware.

related.name: Store
related.text: Simpler shared state when you don't need history.

end.title: Model it once. Undo comes with it.

comingFrom.title: Same concepts, different plumbing.
comingFrom.note: Views become functions, `self.done = …` becomes `self.done.set(…)`, `types.*` becomes initial values or a schema. Both runs print the same final snapshot. The patch differs: MST reports `/todos/0/done`, Pyreon replaces `/todos`.

recipes.title: Undo, and a read-only switch
recipes.text: Snapshots go into an array; undo applies the previous one. One middleware blocks every action while `readOnly` is on.

faq.q: How was it measured against MST?
faq.a: One process per op and library, under bun, in one overnight run that we wrote and judged. Every op in the row is a win, but run it before you rely on it: `packages/fundamentals/state-tree/bench/`.
No. Pyreon components run once and bind each signal read to the DOM node that shows it, so reading `doc.text()` in JSX is all it takes.

faq.q: Can I send patches to a server?
faq.a: Yes: `onPatch` gives `{ op, path, value }` objects as plain JSON, and `applyPatch` applies them on the other side. Only `replace` operations exist.
